instructions: To make the verde sauce: Heat oven to broil. Cut tomatillos in half and place with 6 unpeeled garlic cloves on a baking sheet; broil 5-6 minutes.

In a food processor or blender, add half the roasted tomatillos, all roasted garlic cloves, cilantro, coarsely chopped green onions and peppers, and 1 cup chicken broth. Puree until chunky or smooth as preferred. Set aside. (Prepared salsa verde may substitute this step.)

For the pork stew: Cut meat into 1-2 inch pieces, removing excess fat if very fatty. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a Dutch oven or large skillet over high heat. Sprinkle meat with salt while waiting for oil to heat.

Add pork or beef pieces to the heated pot, working in batches without crowding. Cook until each side browns, turning to brown the opposite side. Remove meat to a plate with a slotted spoon or tongs and cook the remaining batch.
When all meat is browned and removed, lower heat to medium and add chopped onion to the leftover oil; cook about 5 minutes until translucent.
Add spices, stir and cook 1 minute. Return pork to pot with any plate juices. Add 2 cups salsa verde (purchased or homemade) and 1 cup broth; stir and bring to a gentle boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover pot and simmer over medium-low heat about 2 to 2 1/2 hours. Check occasionally and thin with chicken broth if needed.
Serve with accompaniments including sour cream, cilantro sprigs, avocados and limes.
